title: Field position: why a short field turns into points (and how Thursday's fumble became a touchdown)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The original football-film-room repository wasn't reachable (access denied: "not configured for this session"). So there's no new miss of yours to fix, and no snap of yours this connects to yet. This lesson adds a new idea, built on Thursday's Jaguars-Ravens game: three Baltimore turnovers, and where each one left the ball.

The big idea: field position is where a drive starts.The closer to the other team's end zone, the fewer plays you need, and the fewer chances you have to mess up.So a drive that starts at the opponent's 30 scores a TD far more often than one that starts at your own 20.A short field means a drive that starts close. A long field means one that starts far away.

Percentages are rough NFL averages for how often a drive ends in a touchdown, by where it starts (public drive data, rounded). Darker yellow = better odds. A, B and C are plays from Thursday night.

  1. Why closer is so much better. Each set of downs gives the offense 4 tries to gain 10 yards.From your own 20, you need about 8 first downs in a row with no sack, penalty or turnover. From the opponent's 20, you need 2.Every extra play is another chance for a mistake. That's why the shading gets darker as you move right.
  2. A: turnovers give short fields. Baltimore fumbled a kick return in the 4th quarter. Jacksonville took over with a short field.Chris Rodriguez Jr. finished the drive with a 2-yard TD. One mistake, and the Jaguars didn't need a long drive (Sky Sports).Fagnano's 2 interceptions did the same thing: they handed Jacksonville the ball without a punt. Cam Little kicked 4 field goals on drives like that.
  3. B: a short field isn't a sure thing. Baltimore recovered a fumble and got the ball near midfield in the 3rd quarter.It turned it over on downs: 0 points. With a third-string QB, even the middle zone (about 33%) is hard.
  4. C: the exception is the explosive play. Justice Hill ran 65 yards for a TD from his own 35.One big play beats a long field (Lesson 40). That's why a team total can still go over late.
  5. Special teams decide field position too. A 50-yard punt flips the field. A touchback on a kickoff puts the ball at the 35 under the new rules (Lesson 15). A muffed punt is a turnover (Lesson 29).
  6. Same idea in college, bigger numbers. Thursday, Florida Atlantic scored 60 on UTSA. FAU led 21-7 after one quarter.College offenses score more from every zone, so a short field is even more dangerous there.

How to use it in your drill: before each snap, note where the drive started: own 1–20, own 21–40, middle, or opponent's side. Short field (opponent's side): offenses get more aggressive, so expect a deep shot or a 4th-down try (Lesson 38). Backed up inside their own 10: expect a safe run on 1st down, to get room for the punter. Log it next to your run/pass call.

Why it matters for your bets: Unders and team-total Unders lose most often to short fields. A turnover-prone QB (Fagnano Thursday, or Justin Herbert with 10 INTs) helps the other team's Over. Saturday: Ohio State's freshman Luke Fahey against Oregon's defense. If Fahey turns it over, Oregon gets short fields, and your Under 45.5 gets harder.

Real examples to watch (Pacific time): tonight, Nebraska at Illinois (5:00 p.m., FOX): Anthony Colandrea has 5 INTs in three games. Saturday, Oregon at Ohio State (12:30 p.m., CBS) and Penn State at Washington (12:30 p.m., FS1): Penn State is on its backup kicker, so a short field may end in a field-goal try he can't make. Sunday, Texans at Chargers (1:05 p.m., CBS): the Chargers lead the NFL with 17 turnovers.

Video: search YouTube for "field position football explained," "expected points by yard line," and "Jaguars Ravens highlights Week 9 2026."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 6: Situations)

o: A drive that starts close to the other team's end zone
A drive with short passes only
quiz.w: Short field = the drive starts near the opponent's end zone, so it needs fewer plays.

quiz.q: Roughly how often does an NFL drive that starts at the opponent's 20 or closer end in a TD?
quiz.w: The darkest zone in the diagram: about 60%. From your own 20 it's about 15%.

quiz.q: Thursday, a Ravens kick-return fumble led to which play?
quiz.w: Marker A: the turnover gave Jacksonville a short field, and it scored from 2 yards.

quiz.q: In your drill, the offense is backed up at its own 4. What's the most likely 1st-down call?
o: A safe run to get room for the punter
quiz.w: Backed up, offenses avoid risky throws that could mean a safety or a pick in the red zone.
